description: One-sample t-test: statistic t = (mean - mu) / (s / sqrt(n)) and its p-value from Student's t with n - 1 degrees of freedom; alternative -1 less, 0 two-sided, 1 greater

tolerance.reason: For both outputs. The inputs are exact, but t is formed from sums of n rounded terms, so a careful method is off by up to about (kappa_t + n) 2^-53, kappa_t being t's relative condition number in the data and mu (ttest_condition); the p-value adds the factor kappa_p = |t f(t) / P| (at most 99 here). The largest bound max(kappa_p, 1) (kappa_t + n) 2^-53 on this grid is 4.5e-12 (n = 100, loc = 10, mu = 9.99, where t = 0.017 and kappa_t = 4.0e4: mean - mu cancels); 5e-12 is the smallest round value above it (tested). SciPy's worst error is 1.7e-12, at that point

grid: samples x_i = loc + ((7919 i) mod 1000 - 500) / 1000, i = 0..n-1, for n in {2, 3, 5, 10, 30, 100} and loc in {0, 10}; mu = loc + d for d in {-30, -3, -0.3, -0.01, 0.001, 0.1, 1, 10, 100}; each with alternative -1 (less), 0 (two-sided) and 1 (greater). |t| runs from 0.017 to 3410 and the p-value from 4.3e-253 to 1
